clues.name: Police Lockdown
clues.context: The lockdown began at 8:15 PM, well after the bird was last reported heard.
clues.inspectorDescription: The cop sealed the mansion 15 minutes after the 8PM squawk. Whoever hid the bird was already inside long before.

clues.name: PR Disaster
clues.context: The Manager is furious that a missing animal is generating terrible press for his client.
clues.inspectorDescription: Hates animals. Cares only about the Movie Star's brand. Strong feelings, zero evidence.

clues.name: Guest Registry
clues.context: The mansion's sign-in book shows all crew arrivals. One entry reads: D. Marsh — 6:30 PM, half an hour before his cases were officially signed in.
clues.inspectorDescription: He arrived at 6:30. His cases were signed in at 7:00. What was he doing in that thirty minutes?

clues.name: Husband's Grumble
clues.context: The Husband recalls a crew member brushing past him in the hallway at approximately 7:00 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: He didn't catch a name. Just a nervous man with big headphones, in a hurry.

clues.name: D. Marsh — 7:00 PM
clues.context: The delivery manifest lists several crew members. One signed in two sound-proof acoustic cases at exactly 7:00 PM: D. Marsh.
clues.inspectorDescription: D. Marsh. Sound-proof cases. 7:00 PM. Among a list of names — but the only one with cases that block all sound.

clues.name: Sound-Proof Cases
clues.context: The cases are rated for complete acoustic isolation. A bird inside would be completely inaudible.
clues.inspectorDescription: Fully soundproofed. A bird in here could not be heard from next door, let alone down the hall.

clues.name: Star's Ultimatum
clues.context: A handwritten note from the Movie Star to her Husband: 'Derek — Rudebeak woke me up at 5AM. AGAIN. Do SOMETHING about that bird or I am calling my lawyer.'
clues.inspectorDescription: Derek is the Husband's name. He clearly did not do something. Someone else did.

clues.name: New Headphones
clues.context: A freshly opened box of top-of-the-line noise-canceling headphones. The receipt is dated yesterday.
clues.inspectorDescription: He ordered them the day before the shoot. The bird drove him to it. He just handled it more legally than whoever took Rudebeak.

clues.name: 8:00 PM Squawk
clues.context: The Movie Star is certain she heard the bird squawking at exactly 8:00 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: She's sincere. But is it possible she heard a very convincing recording?

clues.name: Broken Latch
clues.context: The cage latch was forcibly broken. Signs suggest the bird was gone well before 8:00 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: That latch was forced open. And those settled feathers aren't fresh. Rudebeak was gone long before the Movie Star heard him.

clues.name: Hidden Speaker
clues.context: A hidden speaker was placed beneath the birdcage, connected to a cable running through the wall.
clues.inspectorDescription: Someone installed this deliberately. The cable goes toward the library. Whatever played through it, it wasn't Rudebeak.

clues.name: Documentary Camera
clues.context: A film crew camera on a tripod with its recording light on, positioned near the birdcage.
clues.inspectorDescription: If this captured anything useful, the Director definitely already watched it and decided not to share.

clues.name: Vocab Ledger
clues.context: A booklet of phrases taught to Rudebeak. The entry for 'garbage slop' is crossed out with 'MAID'S FAULT' written next to it.
clues.inspectorDescription: The Movie Star blames the Maid for teaching Rudebeak the insult. Someone in this house was keeping score.

clues.name: Director's Ratings
clues.context: The Director sees the crisis as a documentary opportunity. He is thrilled.
clues.inspectorDescription: Not a suspect. Just a vulture with a camera. He didn't take the bird — this drama is worth more to him free.

clues.name: Audio Cable
clues.context: An audio cable runs from the mixing board, through the wall, toward the Living Room.
clues.inspectorDescription: That cable goes exactly where the hidden speaker was found. Someone ran a live audio feed from this board to that room.

clues.name: D. Marsh = Sound Guy
clues.context: The Sound Guy's name badge identifies him as D. Marsh — the same name on the bedroom delivery manifest.
clues.inspectorDescription: D. Marsh. On the manifest. In the bedroom at 7PM with sound-proof cases. Now sitting next to a cable that runs to a hidden speaker. He's trying very hard to look calm.

clues.name: Shot List
clues.context: The Director's shot list shows 'Rudebeak reaction shot' was cancelled, with a note in red pen: 'BETTER WITHOUT HIM?'
clues.inspectorDescription: He cancelled the bird's segment. Or someone made him cancel it. And then wrote a very suspicious note about it.

clues.name: The Maid
clues.context: The Maid is furious. She has both a temper and access to every room in the house.
clues.inspectorDescription: Furious. Definitely had a reason to want the bird gone. But wanting something isn't the same as doing it.

clues.name: Insulted Cooking
clues.context: The bird publicly insulted the Maid's cooking. She wrote it down. She drew a skull next to it.
clues.inspectorDescription: A very clear motive. But a note on a fridge is not a crime. Is there anything placing her near the cage?

clues.name: Maid's Paella
clues.context: The Maid's paella is on the stove. It smells extraordinary.
clues.inspectorDescription: For the record: the paella smells incredible. Rudebeak had terrible taste in food criticism.

clues.name: The Gardener
clues.context: The Gardener believes caged animals should be free. He is visibly uncomfortable.
clues.inspectorDescription: He's protesting too much. He had the motive, the tools, and apparently something to hide.

clues.name: Bent Shears
clues.context: The shears show damage consistent with forcing a metal latch. The cage had a snapped latch.
clues.inspectorDescription: These shears snapped the cage latch. The Gardener tried to free the bird. But the bird stayed. So who actually took it?

clues.name: Garden Visit
clues.context: Fresh feathers matching Rudebeak's markings float in the bird bath. He was in the garden this morning.
clues.inspectorDescription: Rudebeak visited the garden this morning. The Gardener would have seen him. Maybe even tried to speak to him before taking more drastic action.

clues.name: Eyewitness — 6:45 PM
clues.context: The Socialite saw a crew member dragging large black cases through the garden at approximately 6:45 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: She saw him. Before 7PM. With cases. Through the garden. Heading toward the house. She didn't think anything of it at the time.

clues.name: Timestamped Photo
clues.context: A timestamped photo places a figure hauling large cases through the garden at 6:47 PM — 13 minutes before the official sign-in.
clues.inspectorDescription: Timestamped. Objective. The figure is blurry but the cases are unmistakable. He was moving through the garden 13 minutes before he officially signed them into the bedroom.

clues.name: Production Schedule
clues.context: The official crew schedule assigns D. Marsh to Library audio setup at 7:00 PM. He was not in the library at 7:00 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: His official assignment was the Library at 7PM. But the manifest says he was in the Bedroom. He wasn't where he was supposed to be.

finalSolveSentence: [WHO] took Rudebeak at [WHEN], hiding the bird inside [WHAT], then played an [HOW] through a [WHERE] to fake an alibi.
